options: Vitamins. Polyamides and vitamins both contain amine linkage.
Proteins. Polyamides and proteins both contain amide linkage.
Vitamins. Polyamides and vitamins both contain amide linkage.
Proteins. Polyamides and proteins both contain amine linkage.
questions.solution:
Correct Option is : (B)
Proteins. Polyamides and proteins both contain amide linkage.

questions.q: Why should the monomers used in addition polymerisation through free radical pathway be very pure?
options: Pure monomers are required to reduce the cost of polymerization.
Pure monomers are required to increase the reaction rate.
Pure monomers are required because even the traces of impurities may act like inhibitors which leads to the formation of polymers with shorter chain length.
Pure monomers are required to enhance the colour of the polymer.
questions.solution:
Correct Option is : (C)
Pure monomers are required because even the traces of impurities may act like inhibitors which leads to the formation of polymers with shorter chain length.

questions.q: Synthetic polymers do not degrade in the environment for a long time. How can biodegradable synthetic polymers be made?
options: By incorporating natural, biodegradable materials into the polymer matrix.
By using non-renewable resources as feedstock.
By increasing the polymer's chemical stability.
By minimizing the exposure of synthetic polymers to environmental factors.
questions.solution:
Correct Option is : (A)
By incorporating natural, biodegradable materials into the polymer matrix.

questions.q: Differentiate between rubbers and plastics on the basis of intermolecular forces.
options: Rubbers have strong intermolecular forces, while plastics have weak forces.
Rubbers are held together by covalent bonds, while plastics are held by van der Waals forces.
Rubbers have weak intermolecular forces and are highly elastic, while plastics have stronger forces and are more rigid.
Rubbers are amorphous, while plastics have a crystalline structure.
questions.solution:
Correct Option is : (C)
Rubbers have weak intermolecular forces and are highly elastic, while plastics have stronger forces and are more rigid.

questions.q: Phenol and formaldehyde undergo condensation to give a polymar (A) which on heating with formaldehyde gives a thermosetting polymer (B). Name the polymers.
questions.solution:
Correct Option is : (A)
‘A’ is novolac and ‘B’ is bakelite

questions.q: What is the main difference between low-density polyethylene (LDPE) and high-density polyethylene (HDPE), both of which are polymers of ethene?
options: LDPE has a higher density than HDPE.
LDPE is more rigid than HDPE.
Low density polythenes are highly branched structures while high density polythene consists of closely packed linear molecules.
LDPE has a higher melting point than HDPE.
questions.solution:
Correct Option is : (C)
Low density polythenes are highly branched structures while high density polythene consists of closely packed linear molecules.

questions.q: Which of the following polymers between bakelite, urea-formaldehyde resin, polythene, polyvinyls and polystyrene soften on heating and harden on cooling? What are the polymers with this property collectively called?
options: Polythene and polystyrene soften on heating and harden on cooling. Such polymers are called thermoplastic polymers.
Polythene, polyvinyls and polystyrene soften on heating and harden on cooling. Such polymers are called thermoplastic polymers.
Polythene, polyvinyls and polystyrene soften on heating and harden on cooling. Such polymers are called thermofibric polymers.
Bakelite, polyvinyls and polystyrene soften on heating and harden on cooling. Such polymers are called thermoplastic polymers.
questions.solution:
Correct Option is : (B)
Polythene, polyvinyls and polystyrene soften on heating and harden on cooling. Such polymers are called thermoplastic polymers.
